_README: CANONICAL REGISTRY. Every reportable number lives here exactly once. Do not restate a value in prose without citing its key. 'verified' = still matches its artifact; 'reproducible' = re-running the pipeline regenerates that artifact. They are independent — several numbers here are verified but NOT reproducible because the OSM network behind them was overwritten (docs/DATA_LOSS_2026-07-24.md). Run scripts/verify_numbers.py to re-check every entry.

lofo_mean_of_folds_auc.caveat: MEAN-OF-FOLDS, not pooled. Pooled OOF AUC is 0.905 and is a DIFFERENT quantity — never present one as the other. Fold sd is 0.107 and the range is 0.682–0.974, so a single-number headline hides a fold that barely beats chance (gangneung_2023 = 0.682).

reproducibility.evidence: tested 2026-08-01: re-ran scripts/run_routing_integration.py; per_fire_auc, pooled_auc, mid/far-band AUC, n_rows and n_positives are all BIT-IDENTICAL to the committed artifact.

lofo_mean_of_folds_auc.notes: Produced by scripts/run_routing_integration.py. The superseded Build-A artifact data/processed/spread_v2/lofo_metrics.json holds a DIFFERENT mean (0.8309) over a DIFFERENT fire set — do not cite it.

lofo_fold_auc_sd.caveat: Sample sd over 6 folds. Not a confidence interval.

reproducibility.evidence: tested 2026-08-01: re-ran scripts/run_routing_integration.py; per_fire_auc, pooled_auc, mid/far-band AUC, n_rows and n_positives are all BIT-IDENTICAL to the committed artifact.

walk_failure_rate_pct.derivation: walk_failures_mobile / n_mobile = 35 / 307, at baseline f=0.3, walk_cutoff=0.5
walk_failure_rate_pct.caveat: Measured among the MOBILE population only, so it is independent of the immobility assumption f. Varies 9.1–17.4 % across the fc sweep; at the baseline cutoff 0.5 the range is 11.3–14.1 %.

check.expr: round(100 * next(r['w'] for r in a if r['immobile_fraction'] == 0.3 and r['walk_cutoff'] == 0.5), 1)

reproducibility.evidence: derived by pure arithmetic from the same four-way counts as rescue_routing.json (scripts/derive_walk_failure.py performs no re-run), so it inherits that artifact's status exactly.

real_roads_both_safe.caveat: Both routers reach a safe refuge. Dominated by the near-static ≥0.5 hazard core.

hazard_npz_sha256.derivation: sha256 of data/processed/routing_demo.npz (the forward-sim hazard field)
hazard_npz_sha256.caveat: The identity of the hazard surface shared by the routing runs. real_roads_real_hazard.json records the same digest at hazard_source.npz_sha256; both must agree.

reproducibility.evidence: tested 2026-08-01: the regenerated npz hashes to d1620f9f…, not 5bed5026…. Cause identified and fully explained: the committed field was built on the FIRE-ACQUISITION bbox (128.97, 36.10, 129.77, 36.90) -> grid 181x147, which reproduces the committed grid_extent EXACTLY. data/raw/firms_data/fire_manifest.json was regenerated 2026-07-23 15:21 with a tighter detection-derived bbox (128.95, 36.20, 129.60, 36.75) -> grid 125x119. The forward simulation itself is unchanged (envelope_area_ha, breadth and drift are all identical).
reproducibility.blocked_by: fire_manifest.json bbox changed 2026-07-23. UNLIKE the OSM loss this is RECOVERABLE: pinning the grid to config bbox.fire_acquisition restores the committed extent. Not changed here — it would alter results and needs a decision.

network_drift_unreachable_delta_pct.caveat: ARM B — a re-run on the 2026-07-24 OSM network. SEPARATE from the committed Round-2 value; never substitute one for the other and never average them. Neither network is 'right'; the reported quantity is SENSITIVITY. 24 -> 32 origins. The most network-sensitive quantity measured: a 0.047 % change in walk-graph nodes moved it 33 %.

check.expr: round(next(r['delta_pct'] for r in a if r['metric'] == 'no_surviving_vehicle_ingress'), 4)

reproducibility.evidence: arm B is regenerable from the snapshotted 2026-07-24 network (data/snapshots/osm-walk_…2bff8d85); arm A is quoted from the committed artifact. Re-running scripts/run_network_drift_experiment.py reproduces the comparison.
